title: reading-notes-llm-inference-marco-diaz
content:
Quick reading notes and scratchpad on LLM inference optimizations - for future experiments on Redwood stack. Informal, incomplete.

Motivation / focus:
- Practical ways to reduce per-token cost and tail latency for generative LLMs without large quality regressions.
- Prioritize techniques that map well to Redwood features: caching, routing, batching, quantization, and model variants/fallbacks.

Papers / posts skimmed (high level):
- FlashAttention family (fast attention kernels): big wins for long sequences and memory efficiency; important when running long-context customers. Implementation considerations: kernel availability per GPU (A100 vs H100), fallback to slower kernels when not supported -> expose in perf profiles.
- Speculative decoding (Zheng et al / DeepSpeed ideas): can reduce latency by using a smaller model to predict token candidates, then verify with the big model. Good for throughput-optimized hosted API and Dedicated where cost matters. Hard bits: consistency, handling deterministic sampling, streaming compatibility.
- KV-cache sharding / offloading papers (techniques to split KV cache across memory types): helps scale to many concurrent sessions with long contexts. Tradeoffs: extra network hops, serialization cost. Evaluate on VPC/private where RDMA available.
- 4-bit/QLoRA quantization blog posts: large accuracy retention on many tasks; quantization profiles differ by model and task. Need eval harness to measure quality regressions on customers' prompt sets (tie to Redwood Optimize).
- Dynamic batching / continuous batching (e.g., Triton inference server ideas): batching improves throughput at cost of latency. Redwood should expose auto policies (latency SLO vs cost).

Conference takeaways (NAI / SysML notes):
- Moving computation earlier (prefix caching + conditional recomputation) reduces repeated attention work for chat histories.
- Observability matters: per-token cost breakdown + hit-rate metrics for prefix caches are critical to evaluate ROI.
- Small-model assistants (e.g., distilled decoders) as front-line validators for safety and hallucination filters before routing to larger models. This maps to Redwood routing policies.

Personal summaries / fragments:
- KV cache hit-rate experiment idea:
  - Instrument calls to measure prefix reuse distribution across customers and routes.
  - Simulate cache sizes to estimate hit-rate vs memory cost; target 60-80% hit-rate for typical chat apps.
  - Measure latency added by cache lookups and possible network overhead if offloaded.

- Quantization rollout plan (draft):
  1) Pick 3 candidate open models (e.g., Llama2-13B, Falcon-40B, Mistral-small)
  2) Create eval suite: summaries, code generation, instruction-following prompts, and domain-specific prompts (internal sample set).
  3) Compare FP16 vs 4-bit (and 8-bit) for speed, memory, and quality -> generate delta metrics and exemplar failures.
  4) If acceptable, create a "quantized" model variant in the catalog and enable routing policy to prefer it under cost-pressure.

- Speculative decoding considerations:
  - Need deterministic verification: if the small model suggests tokens that big model doesn't, fallback cost may erase benefits.
  - Works best with top-k constrained generation; less reliable with sampling-heavy configs.
  - Streaming: must flush verified prefix correctly; can complicate token-at-a-time streaming behavior.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to measure real user prompt distribution to estimate batching windows and cacheability? (sampling privacy-safe headers?)
- For KV offload: which network fabrics are exposed in Private deployments? RDMA/GPUDirect? Add to private-deployments checklist.
- What's the accuracy/cost sweet spot for 4-bit for each model family? Build small automated sweep.
- Can we simulate speculative decoding on Redwood Dedicated with a small-model shadow to get empirical latency/cost numbers?

Immediate experiments to run on Redwood sandbox:
- Run 1k user-chat replay against current hosted Llama2-13B to get prefix reuse distribution and per-token latency breakdown.
- Implement a simple prefix cache shim (local in worker) and measure hit rates and latency delta.
- Quantize a 13B model to 4-bit and run eval suite; log top-10 failure prompts.

Notes for product alignment:
- Observability: expose cache hit-rate, speculative-decoding acceptance rate, and quantized-quality deltas in Redwood Console.
- Routing policies: add heuristics to prefer quantized variants for background jobs and lower-tier customers.
- Rollouts: canary quantized models behind canary traffic split + quality alerts (tie to Redwood Optimize).

Random rough ideas (brain dump):
- "Micro-fallback" concept: for single-token stalls, fall back to smaller model for that token instead of full-response fallback. Risky for coherency but might help tail latency.
- Warm-starting KV caches for returning sessions via persisted session summaries (small embeddings + condensed context) to reduce warmup.

References to save (links above are rough):
- FlashAttention / FlashAttention2 implementations and perf notes (ArXiv + GitHub)
- Speculative decoding / DeepSpeed blog posts
- QLoRA and 4-bit quant blog posts
- Conference slides on inference systems (NAI 2023/2024)

End notes / quick TODO (next week):

- [ ] Prototype local prefix cache in sandbox (Marco + Lena)
- [ ] Create quantization eval harness (Aisha)
- [ ] Sync with private-deployments team about RDMA availability (ask SRE)
